title: Where does an odd overlay land?
fullTitle: FFmpeg overlay on yuv420p: Odd x and y Round Down to Even, and the 4:4:4 Fix Smears the Chroma

thumb.label: OFF BY ONE AT ODD OFFSETS

scenes.narration: You overlay a card at x equals one, y equals one, on yuv four two zero p. Does it land there? A gray base, an eight by eight card with its own color, sixteen offsets from zero to three, f f m peg six point one point one.
captions: Overlay a card at x=1, y=1 on yuv420p.
16 offsets, 0 to 3. Where does it land?

scenes.narration: Reader one is Node: the box of the card in the Y, U and V planes, and the center of its color. Reader two is f f m peg: extractplanes profiles and a checksum per frame. Control: even offsets. Known positive: yuv four four four p.
captions: Node box finder and ffmpeg profiles agree.
Control: even offsets. Known positive: yuv444p.

scenes.narration: Plain overlay does not place the card at an odd offset. X equals one gives zero, x equals three gives two, likewise y. Sixteen offsets make only four frames. Luma and chroma move together, so no color leaks. It is up to one pixel off.
captions: Odd x and y round down to even.

scenes.narration: The usual advice: format equals yuv four four four inside overlay. Now the luma lands exactly, sixteen frames. But the output is yuv four two zero p again, and the chroma comes back smeared: twenty eight to sixty of sixty four card pixels carry the wrong color, and the gray around picks some up.
captions: 28 to 60 of 64 card pixels: wrong color.

scenes.narration: With format equals yuv four two two only x rounds down, y is honored: eight frames. The chroma is smeared too, sixteen to forty eight card pixels wrong.

Stay in yuv four four four p to the end and every offset is exact in all three planes, in both readers. Negative offsets round down too: x minus one and minus two show six of eight columns, minus three shows four.
captions: yuv444p to the end: all 16 exact.

scenes.narration: In yuv four two zero p an odd offset is rounded down,. Use even offsets, or stay in yuv four four four p until the encode. Not tested: other builds, real footage, other formats.
captions: Use even x and y, or stay in 4:4:4.
Not tested: other builds, real footage.
